objective: Prove: (1) every downset of subsets of a finite set is the free-set family of one relation, so the Vamos matroid is carried by single relations, whose laws fail; (2) a top lemma: a subdirect product of finite Mal'tsev algebras, each with a unique maximal congruence, is the full product exactly when its image in the product of the simple tops is full; (3) in a law of a group or a field whose knots compose like cycles, every system's free-set matroid is a direct sum of matroids representable over finite fields, so the Vamos matroid, the non-Pappus matroid and 2-sums of the Fano and non-Fano matroids never appear, nor in shadows, lifts and disjoint unions of such laws; (4) state the remaining converse and its evidence.
status: Proved by MATROID-CONVERSE-20261021-001B-P001 (V1 prose proof with randomized checks; Fleischer's lemma, modularity, Goursat and Scott's lemma cited). Single relations carry any downset of free sets (support relations), including the Vamos matroid, whose relations' laws fail. Top lemma: a subdirect product of Mal'tsev algebras with unique maximal congruences is full exactly when its image in the simple tops is full. So in group laws whose subgroups have unique maximal normal subgroups, every system's matroid is a direct sum of one GF(p)-representable matroid per prime plus parallel classes, and field laws carry F-representable matroids: the Vamos, non-Pappus and Fano-non-Fano 2-sum matroids never occur in them, their shadows, lifts or disjoint unions. Without any difference operation, every pp-definable set of a law composing like cycles has a unique maximal congruence, so tops exist. Open: the matroid-level converse for laws without a difference operation, sharpened to a top lemma for all laws composing like cycles.
title: Proof: difference laws carry only field-representable matroids
